request.input:
Bill number: HB1498
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1487
 By Powers

 HOUSE BILL 1498

 By Reedy

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 16;
 Title 37 and Title 49, relative to student behavior.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 3, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a) This section is known and may be cited as the "Early Behavioral Intervention

 and Reporting Act."

 (b) As used in this section, "early warning signs" means evidence of safety,

 health, or behavioral issues exhibited by a student and includes, but is not limited to,

 indicators of a student engaging in or being the victim of harassment, intimidation,

 bullying, or cyberbullying; making or receiving threats of violence; and exhibiting signs of

 substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal ideation.

 (c) Each LEA and public charter school shall implement a computer-based

 system that teachers and school staff must use to input data of early warning signs

 demonstrated by students enrolled in the LEA or public charter school. Each LEA and

 public charter school shall ensure that each teacher and school staff member is trained

 to identify early warning signs and on how to input data into the computer-based system.

 (d) The computer-based system implemented pursuant to subsection (c) must:

 (1) Align with the harassment, intimidation, bullying, and cyberbullying

 policy adopted by the LEA in accordance with § 49-6-4503; the School Discipline

 Act, compiled in part 41 of this chapter; and with each school safety plan adopted

 by the LEA or public charter school pursuant to the Schools Against Violence in

 Education (SAVE) Act, compiled in part 8 of this chapter;

 (2) Include a database that is capable of receiving and maintaining

 student data entered by teachers and school staff on the early warning signs

 demonstrated by students; and

 (3) Immediately notify the LEA personnel serving on the LEA's threat

 assessment team created pursuant to § 49-6-2701, or the employee of the public

 charter school who is designated to receive such notification, when an early

 warning sign is entered into the system for a student.

 (e) The LEA or public charter school personnel receiving a notification of an

early warning sign of a student pursuant to subdivision (d)(3) shall review the

notification, as well as any other notifications previously received for the student, and

determine whether further action is needed to address the student's behavior.

 (f)

 (1) Each LEA and public charter school shall annually submit a report to

 the department of education that provides the following data collected by the LEA

 or public charter school in the immediately preceding school year:

 (A) The number of early warning signs input into the system;

 (B) The number of early warning signs input into the system,

 disaggregated by the number input by a:

 (i) Teacher, disaggregated further by the grade levels and

 subject areas taught by such teachers; and

 (ii) School staff, disaggregated further by the position,

 assignment, and duties of such school staff;

 (C)

 (i) The number of students for whom more than one (1)

 early warning sign was input into the system; and

 (ii) The number of early warning signs for each student for

 whom more than one (1) early warning sign input into the system;

 (D) A general description of the types of early warning signs input

 into the system; provided, that a description must not include details or

 information that would allow a student to be identified; and

 (E) A general description of the actions taken by the LEA or

 public charter school in response to each early warning sign input into the

 system; provided, that a description must not include details or

 information that would allow a student to be identified.

 (2) Reports provided pursuant to this subsection (f) must not include any

 details or information that would allow a student to be identified.

 (g) Reports made pursuant to this section must comply with the Family

Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) (20 U.S.C. § 1232g); § 10-7-504; the Data

Accessibility, Transparency, and Accountability Act, compiled in chapter 1, part 7 of this

title; and all other relevant privacy laws.

 (h) If the commissioner of education finds that an LEA or public charter school is

not complying with this section, then the commissioner may withhold state funds, in an

amount determined by the commissioner, from the LEA or public charter school until the

LEA or public charter school is in compliance with this section.

 (i) Subsections (c)-(e) do not apply to an LEA or public charter school that

maintains a system for documenting early warning signs demonstrated by students that

was implemented in the LEA or public charter school before July 1, 2026; provided, that

the LEA or public charter school continuously maintains and utilizes the system.

SECTION 2. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill would create the "Early Behavioral Intervention and Reporting Act" for Tennessee public schools. It would require each local education agency (LEA) and public charter school to set up a computer-based system where teachers and school staff must enter "early warning signs" shown by students. The bill defines early warning signs as evidence of safety, health, or behavioral issues. This includes, but is not limited to, signs that a student is involved in or is a victim of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying; is making or receiving threats of violence; or shows signs of substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal ideation. Each LEA and charter school must also train every teacher and staff member to spot early warning signs and to enter data into the system.

The system would have to match the LEA's bullying policy, the School Discipline Act, and each school safety plan under the SAVE Act. It would need a database that can receive and keep the entered student data. It would also have to immediately notify the LEA's threat assessment team, or a designated charter school employee, whenever an early warning sign is entered for a student. The people who get a notice must review it and any earlier notices for that student. They must then decide whether more action is needed to address the student's behavior.

Each LEA and charter school would have to send the Department of Education an annual report covering the prior school year. It would give the total number of early warning signs entered. It would break that number down by teachers (by grade level and subject taught) and by other staff (by position, assignment, and duties). It would give the number of students with more than one sign and the number of signs for each of those students. It would also give a general description of the types of signs and of the actions taken in response. Reports may not include details that could identify a student. They must follow FERPA, section 10-7-504, the Data Accessibility, Transparency, and Accountability Act, and other relevant privacy laws.

If the commissioner of education finds that an LEA or charter school is not complying, the commissioner may withhold state funds, in an amount the commissioner decides, until it complies.

The requirements for the system, training, and review of notices would not apply to an LEA or charter school that already had a system for documenting early warning signs before July 1, 2026, as long as it continuously maintains and uses that system. The bill takes effect July 1, 2026.
</summary>

 and Reporting Act."

claims.claim: The act concerns Tennessee public schools.
claims.summary_quote: for Tennessee public schools
claims.source_quote:
Each LEA and public charter school shall implement a computer-based

 system
claims.rationale: The bill amends Tennessee law and applies its school requirements to LEAs and public charter schools.

claims.claim: LEA stands for local education agency.
claims.summary_quote: local education agency (LEA)
claims.rationale: The supplied text does not expand LEA. This is an explanatory expansion, not a demonstrated change to the bill's legal effect.

claims.claim: Each LEA and public charter school must implement a computer-based system, subject to the later-described exemption.
claims.summary_quote: require each local education agency (LEA) and public charter school to set up a computer-based system
claims.source_quote:
Each LEA and public charter school shall implement a computer-based

 system
claims.rationale: Subsection (c) requires implementation; the summary separately states the grandfathering exemption.

claims.claim: Teachers and school staff must enter students' early warning signs into the system.
claims.summary_quote: teachers and school staff must enter "early warning signs" shown by students
claims.source_quote:
teachers and school staff must use to input data of early warning signs

 demonstrated by students enrolled in the LEA or public charter school
claims.rationale: The summary accurately describes the mandatory data-entry duty.

claims.claim: Early warning signs are evidence of safety, health, or behavioral issues.
claims.summary_quote: early warning signs as evidence of safety, health, or behavioral issues
claims.source_quote:
"early warning signs" means evidence of safety,

 health, or behavioral issues exhibited by a student
claims.rationale: This matches the statutory definition.

claims.claim: The definition nonexclusively includes a student engaging in or being a victim of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying.
claims.summary_quote: This includes, but is not limited to, signs that a student is involved in or is a victim of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying
claims.source_quote:
includes, but is not limited to,

 indicators of a student engaging in or being the victim of harassment, intimidation,

 bullying, or cyberbullying
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the listed conduct, victim status, and nonexclusive nature of the examples.

claims.claim: Making or receiving threats of violence is an early warning sign.
claims.summary_quote: is making or receiving threats of violence
claims.source_quote: making or receiving threats of violence
claims.rationale: Both making and receiving threats are expressly included.

claims.claim: Signs of substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal ideation are included.
claims.summary_quote: shows signs of substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal ideation
claims.source_quote:
exhibiting signs of

 substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal ideation
claims.rationale: The summary reproduces the listed categories.

claims.claim: Each LEA and public charter school must ensure every teacher and staff member is trained to identify early warning signs.
claims.summary_quote: Each LEA and charter school must also train every teacher and staff member to spot early warning signs
claims.source_quote:
Each LEA and

 public charter school shall ensure that each teacher and school staff member is trained

 to identify early warning signs
claims.rationale: The summary captures the universal training requirement, subject to its later-described exemption.

claims.claim: The required training must cover entering data into the system.
claims.summary_quote: and to enter data into the system
claims.source_quote: and on how to input data into the computer-based system
claims.rationale: Data-entry training is expressly required.

claims.claim: The system must align with the LEA's bullying policy.
claims.summary_quote: The system would have to match the LEA's bullying policy
claims.source_quote:
Align with the harassment, intimidation, bullying, and cyberbullying

 policy adopted by the LEA in accordance with § 49-6-4503
claims.rationale: The summary uses bullying policy as shorthand for the specified policy.

claims.claim: The system must align with the School Discipline Act.
claims.summary_quote: the School Discipline Act
claims.source_quote:
the School Discipline

 Act, compiled in part 41 of this chapter
claims.rationale: This is one of the system's expressly required alignments.

claims.claim: The system must align with each school safety plan under the SAVE Act.
claims.summary_quote: each school safety plan under the SAVE Act
claims.source_quote:
with each school safety plan adopted

 by the LEA or public charter school pursuant to the Schools Against Violence in

 Education (SAVE) Act
claims.rationale: The summary accurately identifies the required safety-plan alignment.

claims.claim: The system must include a database capable of receiving and retaining entered student data.
claims.summary_quote: It would need a database that can receive and keep the entered student data
claims.source_quote:
Include a database that is capable of receiving and maintaining

 student data entered by teachers and school staff on the early warning signs

 demonstrated by students
claims.rationale: Receiving and keeping data accurately paraphrases receiving and maintaining it.

claims.claim: The system must immediately notify the LEA's threat assessment team whenever an early warning sign is entered.
claims.summary_quote: immediately notify the LEA's threat assessment team
claims.source_quote:
Immediately notify the LEA personnel serving on the LEA's threat

 assessment team created pursuant to § 49-6-2701
claims.rationale: The bill specifies LEA personnel serving on the team as recipients, not the team as a whole.

claims.claim: For a public charter school, the system must immediately notify its designated employee when an early warning sign is entered.
claims.summary_quote: or a designated charter school employee, whenever an early warning sign is entered for a student
claims.source_quote:
or the employee of the public

 charter school who is designated to receive such notification, when an early

 warning sign is entered into the system for a student
claims.rationale: The designated charter employee and notification trigger match subsection (d)(3).

claims.claim: Personnel receiving a notification must review it.
claims.summary_quote: The people who get a notice must review it
claims.source_quote:
The LEA or public charter school personnel receiving a notification of an

early warning sign of a student pursuant to subdivision (d)(3) shall review the

notification
claims.rationale: Review is mandatory for the receiving personnel.

claims.claim: Personnel must also review earlier notifications for that student.
claims.summary_quote: and any earlier notices for that student
claims.source_quote: as well as any other notifications previously received for the student
claims.rationale: The bill expressly requires review of prior notifications.

claims.claim: Receiving personnel must determine whether further action is needed to address the student's behavior.
claims.summary_quote: They must then decide whether more action is needed to address the student's behavior
claims.source_quote: determine whether further action is needed to address the student's behavior
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the duty to decide, rather than asserting that further action is always required.

claims.claim: Each LEA and public charter school must submit an annual report to the department of education.
claims.summary_quote: Each LEA and charter school would have to send the Department of Education an annual report
claims.source_quote:
Each LEA and public charter school shall annually submit a report to

 the department of education
claims.rationale: The actors, recipient, and annual frequency match.

claims.claim: The annual report covers the immediately preceding school year.
claims.summary_quote: covering the prior school year
claims.source_quote:
data collected by the LEA

 or public charter school in the immediately preceding school year
claims.rationale: The reporting period is accurately stated.

claims.claim: The annual report must give the total number of early warning signs entered.
claims.summary_quote: It would give the total number of early warning signs entered
claims.source_quote: The number of early warning signs input into the system
claims.rationale: This is the required count in subsection (f)(1)(A).

claims.claim: The report must separately count early warning signs entered by teachers.
claims.summary_quote: It would break that number down by teachers
claims.source_quote:
The number of early warning signs input into the system,

 disaggregated by the number input by a:

 (i) Teacher
claims.rationale: The bill requires a teacher-specific breakdown.

claims.claim: Teacher-entered counts must be further broken down by grade level.
claims.summary_quote: by grade level
claims.source_quote:
Teacher, disaggregated further by the grade levels and

 subject areas taught by such teachers
claims.rationale: Grade levels taught are an expressly required reporting dimension.

claims.claim: Teacher-entered counts must be further broken down by subject taught.
claims.summary_quote: and subject taught
claims.source_quote: subject areas taught by such teachers
claims.rationale: Subject areas taught are also required.

claims.claim: The report must separately count early warning signs entered by school staff.
claims.summary_quote: and by other staff
claims.source_quote:
The number of early warning signs input into the system,

 disaggregated by the number input by a:

 (i) Teacher, disaggregated further by the grade levels and

 subject areas taught by such teachers; and

 (ii) School staff
claims.rationale: The summary accurately distinguishes the school-staff reporting category from the teacher category.

claims.claim: School-staff counts must be further broken down by position, assignment, and duties.
claims.summary_quote: by position, assignment, and duties
claims.source_quote:
School staff, disaggregated further by the position,

 assignment, and duties of such school staff
claims.rationale: All three listed reporting dimensions match the bill.

claims.claim: The report must give the number of students with more than one entered early warning sign.
claims.summary_quote: the number of students with more than one sign
claims.source_quote:
The number of students for whom more than one (1)

 early warning sign was input into the system
claims.rationale: The threshold and student count match.

claims.claim: The report must give the number of entered signs for each student with multiple signs.
claims.summary_quote: the number of signs for each of those students
claims.source_quote:
The number of early warning signs for each student for

 whom more than one (1) early warning sign input into the system
claims.rationale: The bill requires a count for each student in the multiple-sign group.

claims.claim: The report must generally describe the types of early warning signs entered.
claims.summary_quote: a general description of the types of signs
claims.source_quote:
A general description of the types of early warning signs input

 into the system
claims.rationale: The description requirement is accurately summarized.

claims.claim: The report must generally describe actions taken in response to early warning signs.
claims.summary_quote: of the actions taken in response
claims.source_quote:
A general description of the actions taken by the LEA or

 public charter school in response to each early warning sign input into the

 system
claims.rationale: The bill expressly requires descriptions of responsive actions.

claims.claim: Reports must not contain information that could identify a student.
claims.summary_quote: Reports may not include details that could identify a student
claims.source_quote:
Reports provided pursuant to this subsection (f) must not include any

 details or information that would allow a student to be identified
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the prohibition on identifying information.

claims.claim: Reports must comply with FERPA.
claims.summary_quote: They must follow FERPA
claims.source_quote:
Reports made pursuant to this section must comply with the Family

Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) (20 U.S.C. § 1232g)
claims.rationale: FERPA compliance is expressly required.

claims.claim: Reports must comply with section 10-7-504.
claims.summary_quote: section 10-7-504
claims.rationale: The bill lists this provision among the mandatory reporting compliance requirements.

claims.claim: Reports must comply with the Data Accessibility, Transparency, and Accountability Act.
claims.summary_quote: the Data Accessibility, Transparency, and Accountability Act
claims.source_quote:
the Data

Accessibility, Transparency, and Accountability Act, compiled in chapter 1, part 7 of this

title
claims.rationale: The named act is expressly included in subsection (g).

claims.claim: Reports must comply with other relevant privacy laws.
claims.summary_quote: and other relevant privacy laws
claims.source_quote: and all other relevant privacy laws
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the additional privacy-law compliance requirement.

claims.claim: The commissioner may withhold state funds upon finding an LEA or public charter school is not complying.
claims.summary_quote: If the commissioner of education finds that an LEA or charter school is not complying, the commissioner may withhold state funds
claims.source_quote:
If the commissioner of education finds that an LEA or public charter school is

not complying with this section, then the commissioner may withhold state funds
claims.rationale: The summary retains both the required finding and the discretionary nature of withholding.

claims.claim: The commissioner determines the amount of state funds withheld.
claims.summary_quote: in an amount the commissioner decides
claims.source_quote:
in an

amount determined by the commissioner
claims.rationale: The bill leaves the amount to the commissioner.

claims.claim: State funds may be withheld until the LEA or public charter school complies.
claims.summary_quote: until it complies
claims.source_quote:
until the

LEA or public charter school is in compliance with this section
claims.rationale: Compliance is the stated endpoint for withholding.

claims.claim: The grandfathering exemption covers the system, training, and notification-review requirements.
claims.summary_quote: The requirements for the system, training, and review of notices would not apply
claims.source_quote: Subsections (c)-(e) do not apply
claims.rationale: Subsections (c)-(e) contain the system, training, notification, and review duties summarized here.

claims.claim: The exemption applies to an LEA or public charter school with an early-warning-sign documentation system implemented before July 1, 2026.
claims.summary_quote: an LEA or charter school that already had a system for documenting early warning signs before July 1, 2026
claims.source_quote:
an LEA or public charter school that

maintains a system for documenting early warning signs demonstrated by students that

was implemented in the LEA or public charter school before July 1, 2026
claims.rationale: The system's function and implementation cutoff match the exemption.

claims.claim: The exemption requires continuous maintenance and use of the existing system.
claims.summary_quote: as long as it continuously maintains and uses that system
claims.source_quote:
provided, that

the LEA or public charter school continuously maintains and utilizes the system
claims.rationale: The summary preserves both continuing conditions.

claims.claim: The act takes effect July 1, 2026.
claims.summary_quote: The bill takes effect July 1, 2026
claims.source_quote: This act takes effect July 1, 2026
claims.rationale: The effective date matches Section 2.
